profile.reading: This building sits within the footprint of the former Loring Air Force Base in Limestone, Maine, now redeveloped as the Loring Commerce Centre, a roughly 3,800 acre commercial, industrial, and aviation park built from the decommissioned base's own buildings and infrastructure. The generic name attached to this listing, simply Datacenter, gives no operator or company identity of its own. The Commerce Centre's published tenant directory lists more than twenty businesses on site, including one technology firm, Lattice Technology Group, an engineering and systems integration consultancy, but Lattice's own description of its work is consulting and architecture design rather than operating server infrastructure or leasing hosting space, and nothing ties that company specifically to this building. Former military bases like Loring often retain purpose built communications or computer rooms from their active service days, structures that sometimes continue in some IT or utility role for a redeveloped site even without becoming a commercial data center business. Given the bare generic tag and the lack of any confirmed operator name tied to this specific structure, this entry is recorded as an unconfirmed building within the Loring Commerce Centre redevelopment, most plausibly a legacy base facility repurposed for some internal IT or utility function, rather than a verified commercial data center.
profile.research_note: Nominatim reverse geocode nearest named place is Loring Job Corps Center, part of the former Loring Air Force Base, now the Loring Commerce Centre redevelopment in Limestone, ME. WebFetch of loringcommercecentre.com and its business directory page confirms the park and lists tenants; only tech-adjacent tenant is Lattice Technology Group (systems integration consulting, latticetech.net), not a data center operator, and not confirmably tied to this specific OSM way. OSM name is the bare generic word "Datacenter" with no operator tag. Plausibly a legacy base comms or utility building repurposed for the industrial park; not a confirmed commercial data center business.

reading.body:
This facility in Aroostook County, Maine is tagged as a data center in OpenStreetMap but carries only a generic name with no operator identified, and published specifications do not exist. Rural northern Maine is not a typical location for commercial data centers, which cluster near major metropolitan fiber routes and population centers. A small facility serving a local telecom carrier, municipal government, or institution is plausible, but the operator and capacity remain unconfirmed.

No power capacity, cooling capacity, or rack density is published for this site. Without those figures, its scale relative to AI infrastructure cannot be assessed. It may be a legacy facility, a municipal installation, or an equipment shelter rather than a hyperscale campus.

Maine has three mapped data center facilities on record and zero published megawatts of capacity across all of them. This site ranks first by published capacity only because that capacity is zero across the state. The facility does not appear in any operator specification data this site has read.
